extension_version.description: The extension version the device's heartbeat reports. Only an extension with a heartbeat sends one, and that heartbeat is what gives the device a new push address once the old one is refused: NULL means an extension too old to recover from that on its own.

file_access.description: Whether the extension may read files on this computer: its "Allow access to file URLs" option in chrome://extensions. A script can attach a file from the reduck folder on the Desktop only when this is true. The heartbeat keeps it current. NULL = the extension did not report it yet.

heartbeat_min.description: Minutes between two heartbeats of a device that has one: what the app asks every extension for, read by whoever judges how long a silence means the device's profile is closed.

last_seen_at.description: When the device last said anything to Reduck (ISO 8601): the extension's heartbeat, a pong, a registration or a push subscription. The heartbeat runs every few minutes while the device's Chrome profile is open, so an old value means that profile is closed, asleep or offline. NULL = the device has not reported since Reduck started recording it.

reachable.description: Whether a wake can be attempted: the device has a Web Push subscription we have not been told is gone. NOT a statement that the browser is running — a push to a closed Chrome is accepted and queued, so this stays true until the subscription is revoked (extension removed, site data cleared, push-service expiry). A run on a device that is `reachable` but shut fails when its browser never answers CDP.
